evidence_note: First-pass source foundation for a tradition that had zero files in this repository before this pass. The strongest material (grade A) comes from Taisho T21 no. 1308, a 9th-century Buddhist-astronomical text ALREADY hash-pinned in this repository by the sukuyodo/ track, re-read here for its Rahu/Ketu computational passages and its twelve-palace list, which the sukuyodo pass explicitly did not extract. The mature-system material (grade D) is transcription-grade, from an anonymous ctext.org wiki page with an unidentified base edition, exactly the evidentiary situation the ziwei/ track already documents for its own comparable transcription. A named, dated 1593 Ming print edition (HathiTrust/University of Michigan) and a separate later compiled edition were both identified and confirmed to survive, but both are access-blocked by unusable OCR, not by rights or language -- no rule rests on either item's OCR text. The Siku Quanshu's own retitled redaction of this tradition, 星命溯源 (1781), independently corroborates two of the ctext transcription's four worked-example fragments, which is real evidence the two texts share a common ancestor. Two findings are flagged as needing primary-source confirmation in the next pass despite currently resting on secondary synthesis: the three-era Rahu/Ketu redefinition history, and the twelve-branch planetary rulership scheme's exact structural match to the Hellenistic domicile table. Nothing here is customer-eligible.

rules.period: 9th century CE Tang translation of an Indian nine-luminary source; the sole surviving textual layer before the mature Song-era four-surplus system

scope.unit: definition and function

conditions.trigger: identifying what Rahu (羅睺遏囉師) is and does in the nine-luminary system
conditions.stated_behavior: constantly moves hidden and unseen (常隱行不見); when it meets Sun or Moon at new or full moon, or is in opposition to them, an eclipse results

conclusion.chinese: 羅睺遏羅師者，一名黃幡，一名蝕神頭，一名複，一名太陽首，常隱行不見。逢日月則蝕，朔望逢之必蝕，與日月相對亦蝕。
conclusion.engine_rendering: Rahu-graha is also called the Yellow Banner, also called the Eclipse-Deity's Head, also called Fu, also called the Sun's Head. It constantly moves hidden and unseen. When it meets the Sun or Moon, there is an eclipse; meeting them at new or full moon there is certainly an eclipse; being opposite Sun and Moon also causes eclipse.
conclusion.function: establishes Rahu's identity as an invisible eclipse-causing point tied to the lunar nodes, not a physical body

rules.period: 9th century CE Tang translation of an Indian nine-luminary source; the sole surviving textual layer before the mature Song-era four-surplus system

scope.unit: the text's own comparison of two eclipse theories

conditions.trigger: the text explicitly compares two rival explanations of eclipse causation
conditions.theory_1: the Indian theory (attributed to 婆毘磨's calculation method), under which Rahu itself is the eclipse-causing point
conditions.theory_2: the native "Han" (Chinese) theory: Sun and Moon share one path; the Moon covers the Sun causing a solar eclipse; opposite the Sun there is a shadow-point 暗虛 the size of the Sun, and when the Moon meets it there is a lunar eclipse

conclusion.chinese: 謹按天竺婆毘磨步之云爾。漢說云日月同道，月掩日而日蝕。天對日衝，其大如日，日光不照，謂之暗虛，暗虛值月而月蝕。二說不同。今按天竺曆，得其正理矣。
conclusion.engine_rendering: Respectfully, according to the Indian [authority] Poupimo's calculational method, it is said thus. The Han account says: Sun and Moon share one path; the Moon covers the Sun and there is a solar eclipse. Heaven's point opposite the Sun is as large as the Sun; where the Sun's light does not shine, it is called the Dark Void; when the Dark Void meets the Moon, there is a lunar eclipse. The two accounts differ. Now, checking against the Indian calendrical method, [we find] it has the correct principle.
conclusion.function: an explicit, dated (9th century) instance of a Chinese astronomical text naming a native theory and an imported theory side by side and stating a preference for the imported one on its own authority
conclusion.distinctiveness: this passage is why the pack does not treat Qizheng Siyu's syncretism as a modern inference: the source text argues its own syncretism explicitly

exceptions: 婆毘磨 (transliterated here as 'Poupimo') is not confidently identified with a specific named Indian astronomer in this pass; it is preserved as the text's own transliteration rather than resolved to a modern identification.

rules.period: 9th century CE Tang translation of an Indian nine-luminary source; the sole surviving textual layer before the mature Song-era four-surplus system

scope.unit: motion rate and cycle length

conditions.trigger: computing Rahu's position and cycle from the text's own stated rates

stated_rates.per_18_years: one circuit of heaven, short by 11 and 2/3 degrees
stated_rates.per_93_years: one Great Cycle (大終), beginning again

conclusion.chinese: 常逆行於天，行無徐疾。十九日行一度，一月行一度十分度之六，一年行十九度三分度之一，一年半行一次。十八年一周天退十一度三分度之二。凡九十三年一大終而復始。
conclusion.engine_rendering: It always moves retrograde in the heavens, its motion without slow or fast [variation]. In 19 days it moves 1 degree; in 1 month it moves 1 and 6/10 degrees; in 1 year it moves 19 and 1/3 degrees; in 1.5 years it moves through one zodiacal house. In 18 years it completes one circuit of heaven, retrograding short by 11 and 2/3 degrees. In total, 93 years constitutes one Great Cycle, and it begins again.
conclusion.arithmetic_check: recomputing from the stated annual rate: 93 years x 19+1/3 deg/year = 1798.33 degrees = 4.995 complete retrograde circuits, i.e. the 93-year Great Cycle is very close to (within about 2 degrees of) exactly five complete revolutions at the stated annual rate. The stated 18-year/11+2/3-degree figure is NOT perfectly consistent with the stated annual rate taken alone: 19+1/3 deg/year x 18 years = 348 degrees exactly, implying a 12-degree shortfall rather than the stated 11+2/3 degrees -- a small (~1/3 degree) internal inconsistency, recorded honestly rather than silently corrected.
conclusion.real_astronomy_note: the real lunar nodal precession period is approximately 18.6 tropical years; the text's own numbers, taken as a system rather than any single stated figure in isolation, are consistent with a real, sophisticated observational basis for this figure, not an arbitrary round number.

exceptions: The 18-year/11+2/3-degree shortfall figure does not arithmetically match the stated 19+1/3-degrees-per-year rate exactly; this pack records both stated figures as given rather than picking one as correct.

rules.period: 9th century CE Tang translation of an Indian nine-luminary source; the sole surviving textual layer before the mature Song-era four-surplus system

scope.unit: definition and function

conditions.trigger: identifying what Ketu (計都遏囉師) is and does in the nine-luminary system
conditions.stated_behavior: constantly moves hidden and unseen; when it reaches a person's natal palace there is disaster, or when hidden/blocked this is the most severe affliction; it moves PROGRADE (順行), explicitly contrasted with Rahu's stated retrograde motion

conclusion.chinese: 計都遏囉師，一名豹尾，一名蝕神尾，一名月勃力，一名太陰首。常隱行不見，到人本宮則有災禍，或隱覆不通為厄最重。常順行於天，行無徐疾。
conclusion.engine_rendering: Ketu-graha is also called the Leopard's Tail, also called the Eclipse-Deity's Tail, also called Yuebo-li, also called the Moon's Head. It constantly moves hidden and unseen; when it reaches a person's natal palace there is disaster, or hidden and blocked, this is the most severe affliction. It always moves prograde (direct) in the heavens, its motion without slow or fast [variation].
conclusion.function: establishes Ketu, in this text, as a body moving in the OPPOSITE sense from Rahu (prograde vs retrograde), paired with Rahu as Moon's-Head to Rahu's Sun's-Head, not as Rahu's 180-degree opposite point on a shared axis
conclusion.distinctiveness: the alternate name 月勃力 (Yuebo-li) differs from 月孛 (Yuebei), the name the mature Qizheng Siyu four-surplus system uses for the lunar apogee, by one syllable rendered with a near-homophone character (勃 vs 孛). Combined with the motion data in the companion rule qizheng.t1308.ketu_prograde_period_and_arithmetic, this is the textual basis for concluding (see qizheng.boundary.t1308_ketu_is_later_yuebei_not_a_node) that this text's Ketu and the mature system's Yuebei are the same astronomical referent under two names from two textual layers.

rules.period: 9th century CE Tang translation of an Indian nine-luminary source; the sole surviving textual layer before the mature Song-era four-surplus system

scope.unit: motion rate and cycle length

conditions.trigger: computing Ketu's position and cycle from the text's own stated rates

stated_rates.per_9_years: one circuit of heaven, over by 6 and 3/10 degrees
stated_rates.per_62_years: seven circuits of heaven, over by 3 and 4/10 degrees

conclusion.chinese: 九日行一度，一月行三度十分度之四，九月行一次，一年行四十度十分度之七。凡九年一周天差六度十分度之三，凡六十二年七周天差三度十分度之四。
conclusion.engine_rendering: In 9 days it moves 1 degree; in 1 month it moves 3 and 4/10 degrees; in 9 months it moves through one zodiacal house; in 1 year it moves 40 and 7/10 degrees. In total, 9 years is one circuit of heaven, exceeding by 6 and 3/10 degrees; in total, 62 years is seven circuits of heaven, exceeding by 3 and 4/10 degrees.
conclusion.arithmetic_check: both closing figures check EXACTLY against the stated annual rate with no rounding slack: 40.7 deg/year x 9 years = 366.3 degrees = 360 + 6.3 degrees, matching the stated 9-year excess exactly; 40.7 deg/year x 62 years = 2523.4 degrees = (7 x 360) + 3.4 degrees, matching the stated 62-year excess exactly. This is a cleanly self-consistent set of figures, in contrast to the small internal inconsistency recorded for Rahu in qizheng.t1308.rahu_retrograde_period_and_arithmetic.
conclusion.real_astronomy_note: solving 360 / 40.7 gives a period of approximately 8.845 years, within roughly half a day of the real astronomical lunar apsidal (apogee) precession period of approximately 8.85 years -- strong internal evidence that this passage's referent is the lunar apogee, not an arbitrary or nodal point.

rules.period: encoder's inference, drawn 2026-08-02 from the two T1308 rules above

scope.unit: cross-layer boundary rule

conditions.trigger: the pack must state clearly whether T1308's 計都 (Ketu) and the mature Qizheng Siyu system's 月孛 (Yuebei) are the same referent
evidence_for_identity: T1308's Ketu carries the alternate name 月勃力 (Yuebo-li), a near-homophone of 月孛 (Yuebei)
T1308's Ketu moves prograde at a rate whose implied period (~8.845 years) matches the real lunar apsidal precession period (~8.85 years) almost exactly
modern secondary synthesis (zh.wikipedia, citing 陳于柱 2009) independently states that early transmission defined 計都 as the Moon's apogee, matching this reading
evidence_against_conflation: T1308 never uses the label 月孛 anywhere in the passages read in this pass
T1308 is a nine-luminary (九曜) system with no fourth or fifth surplus body at all -- it has no place for a separate Ziqi or a separate Yuebei alongside Rahu and Ketu
the mature system's own Ketu is commonly treated as a nodal point paired with Rahu (per the same secondary synthesis, describing a Tang-Song redefinition), which is NOT what T1308's Ketu is

conclusion.judgment: this pack treats T1308's Ketu and the mature system's Yuebei as the same underlying astronomical referent (the lunar apogee) carried under two names across two textual layers, and treats T1308's Ketu and the MATURE system's Ketu as two different referents despite sharing one name across those same two layers
conclusion.status_of_this_conclusion: an encoder's inference from textual and arithmetic evidence, not a claim any single source makes about itself. It is stated here as a hypothesis this pack commits to for internal consistency, not as settled fact
conclusion.practical_consequence: no rule in this pack merges T1308's Ketu-passage content into a rule labeled qizheng's mature-system Ketu, and no rule merges it OUT of a rule labeled Yuebei. The boundary is enforced by school_id: T1308 material stays under school_id qizheng_t1308_extraction and is never backfilled into ctext- or Siku-Quanshu-sourced Yuebei or Ketu material

rules.period: documented transitions: 9th c. (Tang translation), late Tang/early Song, early Qing (Schall von Bell reform, 17th c.)

scope.unit: definitional history across three eras

conditions.trigger: determining which node Rahu and Ketu name at a given point in the tradition's history
conditions.era_1_9th_c: per T1308: Rahu = eclipse-causing retrograde point (see qizheng.t1308 rules); Ketu = lunar apogee (see qizheng.t1308 rules); NOT a paired-node system at all
conditions.era_2_tang_song_transition: Rahu and Ketu re-paired as opposed lunar nodes: Rahu becomes the descending node (交初), Ketu the ascending node (交中)
conditions.era_3_qing_schall_reform: 湯若望's 新法 (New Method) swaps the pairing to match the modern Western/Vedic convention: Rahu = ascending node, Ketu = descending node -- but working fate-calculators largely kept the era-2 convention rather than adopting the court's astronomical reform

conclusion.judgment: as a consequence, the CURRENT convention in practicing Qizheng Siyu circles for Rahu and Ketu is reported to be the mirror image of the modern Western and Jyotisha convention: Rahu = descending node, Ketu = ascending node
conclusion.practical_consequence: an implementation that silently applies the Western/Jyotisha node convention (Rahu=ascending) to a Qizheng Siyu chart would invert the entire Rahu/Ketu axis relative to what a Qizheng Siyu practitioner expects. This must be an explicit, disclosed configured_method choice, never a silent default
conclusion.evidence_status: this claim is sourced from a modern secondary synthesis (zh.wikipedia) citing named academic scholarship (陳于柱 2009 on a Dunhuang manuscript, 《推人九天宮法》); neither the Song-era text establishing era 2 nor the Qing-era 新法 material for era 3 was independently retrieved and read in this pass

exceptions: The era-1 to era-2 transition is not itself independently verified against a primary Song-dynasty text in this pass; only era 1 (via T1308) is independently primary-verified in this pack.

scope.unit: stated period and its epistemic status

conditions.trigger: computing or characterizing Ziqi's position and cycle
conditions.stated_period_source_b: 29 years per circuit of heaven, with finer rates of 29 days/degree and 29 months/palace
conditions.stated_absence: no corresponding astronomical phenomenon has been identified for this body by modern scholarship

conclusion.judgment: Ziqi's period is inconsistently reported as 28 or 29 years across modern sources, and unlike Rahu (a real geometric node) and Ketu/Yuebei (the real lunar apogee), Ziqi has NO identified real astronomical referent at all
conclusion.theorized_origin_1: the 19-year/7-intercalation lunisolar leap-month cycle, scaled up (19-year cycle has 7 intercalary months; ~28 years would have roughly 10 intercalations on the same ratio)
conclusion.theorized_origin_2: modeled on the Tai Sui (太歲, the counter-Jupiter duodecennial year-counter) system's structure, extended from 12 branches/12 years to 28 lunar mansions/28 years
conclusion.epistemic_disclosure_required: Ziqi should be disclosed to a reader as a calendrical bookkeeping construct given a planetary personality, of a genuinely different epistemic status from the other three surplus bodies and the seven visible governors -- not silently presented as 'a fourth planet' on equal footing

exceptions: The 28-year and 29-year figures are both reported in modern sources with no resolution attempted in this pass; this pack records the disagreement rather than choosing a side.
Neither theorized origin is confirmed against a primary text in this pass.

scope.unit: elemental-affinity naming scheme for the four surplus bodies

conditions.trigger: explaining why each of the four surplus bodies carries its name, via a five-phase (五行) elemental-surplus logic distinct from their astronomical computation

stated_correspondences.月孛 (Yuebei): the surplus of Water (孛為水餘)
stated_correspondences.紫氣 (Ziqi): the surplus of Wood (氣乃木餘)
stated_correspondences.羅睺 (Rahu): the surplus of Fire (羅乃火餘)
stated_correspondences.計都 (Ketu): the surplus of Earth (計乃土餘)

conclusion.chinese: 水之餘孛也，孛為水餘，木之餘氣也，氣乃木餘，火之餘羅也，羅乃火餘，土之餘計也，計乃土餘
conclusion.engine_rendering: Bo [Yuebei] is Water's surplus, [so] Qi [in 'Bo' the character group] is Water's surplus; Qi [Ziqi] is Wood's surplus, [so] Qi is Wood's surplus; Luo [Rahu] is Fire's surplus, [so] Luo is Fire's surplus; Ji [Ketu] is Earth's surplus, [so] Ji is Earth's surplus.
conclusion.function: this is a DIDACTIC/mnemonic naming scheme (each surplus body named for the five-phase element it is said to be 'left over' from), and this pack does not treat it as astronomically causal. It is explicitly a different layer from the T1308 computational passages (qizheng.t1308.* rules), which state real motion rates with no reference to this elemental logic
conclusion.distinctiveness: note the mismatch with Saturn's real ~29.46-year sidereal period sometimes loosely associated with 'the 29-year Ziqi cycle' reported elsewhere in modern secondary sources (see qizheng.secondary.ziqi_period_and_no_astronomical_referent): this elemental scheme pairs Ziqi with Wood/Jupiter, not Earth/Saturn, which is internally consistent with (though not proof of) the modern secondary claim that Ziqi's period has no real astronomical grounding at all

scope.unit: the tradition's own stated ranking of the seven governors versus the four surplus

conditions.trigger: establishing which class of body a chart-reader should treat as primary when the two classes conflict
conditions.stated_class_a: 七政 (the seven governors) are likened to gentlemen (君子) among people
conditions.stated_class_b: 四曜 (the four surplus) are mere left-over qi (餘氣耳); Fire/Rahu, Ketu, and Bo/Yuebei specifically are likened to petty men (小人)

conclusion.chinese: 七政猶人中之君子也...四曜乃餘氣耳...以火、羅、計、孛為小人
conclusion.engine_rendering: The seven governors are like the gentlemen among people... the four luminaries are mere surplus qi... [the tradition] takes Fire, Rahu, Ketu, and Bo [Yuebei] as petty men.
conclusion.function: this is the tradition's own stated judgment hierarchy at the class level: the seven real bodies take precedence in dignity and are judged first; the four surplus bodies are structurally secondary, auxiliary afflicting/mitigating factors, not co-equal chart rulers
conclusion.note: Fire (Mars) appearing in the 'petty men' list alongside three of the surplus bodies is the source's own grouping, not an error introduced by this encoding; it is preserved as stated

scope.unit: directional asymmetry of affliction between the two classes

conditions.trigger: judging an affliction/aspect relationship between one of the seven governors and one of the four surplus bodies
conditions.case_a: one of the seven governors afflicts (克, 'conquers' in five-phase terms) a surplus body
conditions.case_b: a surplus body afflicts one of the seven governors

conclusion.chinese: 寧五星犯餘氣...寧可我去克他。莫餘氣犯五星...為餘氣所犯，必大有凶害
conclusion.engine_rendering: Better that one of the five stars offends the surplus qi... better that I go and conquer it. Let it not be that the surplus qi offends the five stars... to be offended by the surplus qi will certainly bring great misfortune and harm.
conclusion.judgment: case_a is tolerable (the dignified body's own affliction of a surplus body is not itself alarming); case_b is the tradition's own worst-case configuration (a surplus body afflicting a real governor is stated to bring severe misfortune)
conclusion.function: this is a direct, explicit, source-stated judgment-hierarchy rule: the direction of an affliction between the two classes changes its severity, not merely which planet is 'stronger'

rules.period: delineation of a historical Tang figure (張巡, 709-757 CE)

scope.figure: 張巡 (Zhang Xun, general, died defending Suiyang)
scope.unit: delineation fragment checked against a real historical outcome

conditions.trigger: the source's own worked-example chart for Zhang Xun
conditions.stated_placement: life sits at Heart-Moon-Fox (心月狐); the limit-period in question passes through Extended-Net-Moon-Deer (張月鹿); Saturn ahead, Ketu behind (土前計後)
conditions.stated_historical_check: he did indeed die at [An] Lushan's soldiers' hands (果死祿山兵手)

conclusion.chinese: 彼命坐心月狐，今限歷張月鹿...土前計後...果死祿山兵手
conclusion.engine_rendering: His life sits at Heart-Moon-Fox; the present limit-period passes through Extended-Net-Moon-Deer... Saturn ahead, Ketu behind... he did indeed die at [An] Lushan's soldiers' hands.
conclusion.reproducibility_status: NOT machine-checkable in this pass: no structured birth data located. However, the source's own claimed check -- that this configuration corresponds to death at An Lushan's forces' hands -- is checkable against real, independently documented history: Zhang Xun died in 757 CE after the fall of Suiyang during the An Lushan rebellion, which is exactly the outcome the delineation claims
conclusion.significance: this is the strongest single piece of evidence in this pass that the worked examples are not free invention: the claimed correspondence between chart configuration and a specific, well-documented historical death is a testable claim in principle, even though this pass cannot yet test it end-to-end without Zhang Xun's birth data

exceptions: The animal/element mansion labels (心月狐, 張月鹿) belong to the 七曜禽星 twenty-eight-mansion elemental-animal correspondence scheme; this pack does not attempt to reconstruct that full scheme from this one fragment.

scope.unit: the Siku editors' own account of the 'Guo Lao' school name

conditions.trigger: the Siku Quanshu editors' abstract explains why this school of five-star fate-calculation carries Zhang Guo's name
conditions.stated_position: the art is attributed to (依托于) Zhang Guo; practitioners consequently named this school after 'Guo Lao's Five Stars'

conclusion.chinese: 以五星推命之學依托于張果，術者遂以果老五星自名一家
conclusion.engine_rendering: The art of five-star fate-calculation is attributed to Zhang Guo; practitioners therefore named this school after Guo Lao's Five Stars.
conclusion.function: an official, dated (1781) acknowledgment that 'Guo Lao' / 'Zhang Guo' branding is a school-naming convention layered onto the technique, not a claim the imperial editors themselves endorsed as personal authorship by the historical or legendary Zhang Guo
conclusion.distinctiveness: this is the closest analogue in this pack to the byzantine/ track's finding that a Byzantine attribution is a reading habit, not evidence of authorship: here it is the imperial editors making exactly that distinction, in their own official capacity, about their own included text

scope.unit: the work's five-juan structure and its own transmission legend

conditions.trigger: documenting the five-juan structure and noting an internal anachronism in the transmission story juan 2 tells about itself
conditions.juan_1: 通元遺書雜錄, three sections attributed to Tang-era Zhang Guo
conditions.juan_2: 果憕問答, four sections, framed as the direct oral instruction (口授) of Zhang Guo received by a named interlocutor (李憕)
conditions.juan_3: 元妙經解, attributed to Zhang Guo's composition with 鄭希誠's commentary
conditions.internal_anachronism: the interlocutor named in juan 2 is placed in the Ming dynasty, receiving direct oral instruction from a Tang-dynasty immortal -- an anachronism internal to the text's own transmission legend

conclusion.judgment: the work's own transmission story is legendary/hagiographic on its face (a centuries-later interlocutor meeting a Tang-era immortal in person), and the Siku editors evidently let this stand rather than correcting or flagging it in the abstract this pack located
conclusion.function: this pack does not treat the juan-2 dialogue as historical testimony about an actual Ming-dynasty meeting; it treats it as source content whose own internal chronology is not self-consistent, exactly the caution the byzantine/ track applies to Byzantine attribution claims

exceptions: The exact identity and dates of 李憕 as named in this text were not independently verified in this pass; the anachronism is flagged regardless because a real Ming-dynasty Li Cheng meeting a person active in the Tang dynasty (713-742 CE) is impossible on its face however 李憕 is identified.

This class [of body] is best taken singly; it fears being mixed together.
conclusion.function: independently corroborates qizheng.guolaoxingzong.four_surplus_prefer_solitary_placement from a second, better-provenanced witness (the Siku Quanshu redaction), strengthening confidence that this principle belongs to the shared ancestral tradition rather than to one transcription's idiosyncrasy

rules.period: 9th century CE Tang translation of an Indian nine-luminary source; the sole surviving textual layer before the mature Song-era four-surplus system

scope.unit: the earliest attested twelve-palace name list in this pack

conditions.trigger: listing the twelve palaces as attested in the 9th-century nine-luminary layer, under the heading 七曜旁通九執至行年法

conclusion.engine_rendering: Life, Wealth, Siblings, Estate, Children, Servants, Spouse/Consorts, Illness, Travel, Rank, Fortune, Poverty/Hardship -- twelve palaces, in this order, under a heading translating as 'The method by which the seven luminaries interpenetrate the nine seizers, extended to the directed-year technique.'
conclusion.function: establishes that the twelve-palace scheme itself predates the mature 'Guo Lao' systematization by centuries and is not a later Song/Ming invention layered onto an imported nine-luminary core; only the specific palace names and their number-11 (福相/Fortune) and number-12 (困窮/Poverty) framing differ somewhat from the mature system, see qizheng.boundary.twelve_palace_name_continuity_and_drift

scope.unit: boundary rule comparing the 9th-century and mature palace-name lists

conditions.trigger: comparing the T1308 twelve-palace list against the mature system's list as attested in the ctext.org transcription's juan-2 pattern catalogue

conclusion.judgment: ten of twelve palace names are stable or trivially synonymous across nine centuries of transmission (財宮/財帛, 僮僕/奴僕, 妻妾/夫妻, 疾病/疾厄, 官位/官祿, 福相/福德); the twelfth palace's name shifts from 困窮 ('Poverty/Hardship') in the 9th-century layer to 相貌 ('Appearance') in the mature system -- a genuine semantic change this pack records rather than resolves, since no intermediate witness was read in this pass
conclusion.practical_consequence: no rule in this pack merges the T1308 twelfth-palace significations into a rule about the mature system's twelfth palace, or vice versa, given the documented name change

scope.unit: domicile/rulership of the twelve branches, and its exact structural match to the Hellenistic domicile table

conditions.trigger: assigning a ruling planet to each of the twelve branches (which double as the twelve palace positions and, via the standard branch-zodiac correlation, the twelve zodiacal signs)

conclusion.judgment: under this correlation, the stated scheme maps EXACTLY onto the Ptolemaic/Hellenistic domicile table with zero deviation: Sun/Leo, Moon/Cancer, Mercury/Gemini+Virgo, Venus/Taurus+Libra, Mars/Aries+Scorpio, Jupiter/Sagittarius+Pisces, Saturn/Capricorn+Aquarius
conclusion.significance: if confirmed against a primary Qizheng Siyu text, this is the single strongest piece of evidence in this pass for the tradition's stated Hellenistic/Indian syncretic transmission: not a vague family resemblance, but an exact, checkable, structural transplant of a named foreign technical system onto Chinese branch nomenclature
conclusion.evidence_status: sourced from modern web secondary material (getit01.com, baike.baidu.com), not yet located inside 張果星宗 or 星命溯源 directly in this pass. The cross-check against the Hellenistic table is this pack's own derived computation, not a claim any source makes explicitly

exceptions: No primary Qizheng Siyu classical text was located stating this rulership scheme directly in this pass; it is graded D specifically because of that gap despite the scheme's internal coherence and consistency across independent modern sources.

rules.period: structural comparison, not tied to a single historical period

scope.unit: differentiating Qizheng Siyu from the two other Chinese traditions already built in this repository

conditions.trigger: a reader or implementer might conflate Qizheng Siyu with BaZi (八字) or Zi Wei Dou Shu (紫微斗數), the two other Chinese traditions already built in docs/research/multitradition/
conditions.bazi_structure: pure sexagenary (stem-branch) pillars for year/month/day/hour; no real planetary positions; no zodiac signs; no houses in the Western sense
conditions.ziwei_structure: fourteen catalogued main stars plus dozens of auxiliaries placed into twelve palaces by lunar-calendar-keyed lookup tables; the star positions are NOT real planetary or stellar positions -- Zi Wei itself is not a real star whose position is computed astronomically
conditions.qizheng_structure: the seven visible classical bodies (Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) at their REAL computed ecliptic positions, plus four calculated invisible points (Rahu, Ketu, Ziqi, Yuebei) at ASTRONOMICALLY-DERIVED positions (nodes, apogee, and a calendrical construct respectively), placed into a twelve-sign zodiac and a twelve-house Western-style chart structure

conclusion.judgment: Qizheng Siyu is the only one of the three Chinese traditions in this repository that casts a chart using real or astronomically-derived celestial positions in a zodiac-and-houses structure; BaZi uses no celestial positions at all, and Zi Wei uses a star catalogue with no real celestial positions
conclusion.practical_consequence: no rule, table, or worked example may be shared or backfilled between the qizheng/, bazi/, and ziwei/ directories in this repository; each is its own school_id space with its own source registry entries

rules.period: Ming Wanli 1593 print versus a later (post-1912, through at least 1926) compiled Republican edition

scope.unit: keeping the two identified print traditions of 張果星宗/果老星宗 separate

conditions.trigger: two distinct physical print traditions of this work were identified in this pass, both surviving only as unusable OCR
conditions.witness_1: the Ming Wanli 21 (1593) Nanjing Dawentang print (Internet Archive item guolaoxingzong), ten juan including a 鄭氏星案 appendix
conditions.witness_2: a later compiled edition (Internet Archive item glxz1) whose preface names a running 量天尺 astronomical conversion table revised across reigns from the Kangxi era through 1926, credited in part to Republic-era astronomer 高魯

conclusion.judgment: these are two different print traditions separated by roughly 330 years and carrying materially different apparatus (the later one adds a multi-reign astronomical conversion table absent from the earlier one's ten-juan structure); no content from one may be silently attributed to the other
conclusion.practical_consequence: both are registered as separate source_registry entries and neither is used as a controlling edition for any rule in this pack, since both survive here only as unusable OCR
